cards.text: The writer of Hebrews is writing to fellow believers (Hebrews 3:1), and he's just spent a whole chapter showing that Jesus is a priest forever (Hebrews 7:17). Now he cuts straight to the point: we really do have a high priest like that. Friend, when somebody says 'here's the point,' that's when I stop sneaking cookie dough and LISTEN.

cards.question: The writer of Hebrews says we really do have a high priest, Jesus, a priest forever. Where did He sit down?

answers.text: At the right hand of God's throne in heaven
Beside the altar in the temple courts
On Mount Sinai with the seventy elders

cards.text: He's seated, and He's STILL on the job: He ministers in the sanctuary, the true tabernacle. Meanwhile, I sit down for one second and three trays of cookies burn.

cards.question: True or false: The true tabernacle where Jesus ministers was set up by man.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: So what does a high priest actually DO all day? The writer lays out the job description, plain and simple.

cards.question: According to the writer, what is every high priest appointed to do?

answers.text: Offer both gifts and sacrifices
Guard the ark of the covenant
Lead the army into battle

cards.text: So Jesus, as High Priest, had to have something to offer too. Now here's a twist: on earth, there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says that if Jesus were on earth, He would still serve as a priest there.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: So what about the place where those earthly priests serve? The writer has something to say about it.

cards.question: How does the writer describe the place where the earthly priests serve?

answers.text: A copy and shadow of what is in heaven
A gate that opens straight into heaven
A throne room filled with heaven's glory

cards.question: When Moses, Israel's leader, was about to build the tabernacle, he was warned to make everything just right. What did he have to follow?

answers.text: The pattern shown him on the mountain
The design King David gave Solomon
The measurements shown Ezekiel in a vision

cards.text: But now Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry. Friend, a cookie's shadow on the wall looks GREAT, but try taking a bite out of it.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says the covenant Jesus mediates is founded on better promises.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: So why a new covenant at all? The writer reasons it out: if that first covenant had been without fault, nobody would have gone looking for a second one.

cards.question: The first covenant had a problem. The writer says God found fault with the ___.

answers.text: people
prophets
angels

cards.text: Then the writer quotes God's words, first spoken through the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 31:31): "Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant…" Friend, this is the big promise, so I'm putting my whisk DOWN.

cards.question: True or false: God says He will make this new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: God says the new one won't be like the covenant He made with their fathers, back when He took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt.

cards.question: God made a covenant with the fathers of Israel and Judah when He led them out of Egypt. What did those fathers do with that covenant?

answers.text: They did not abide by it
They kept it for generations
They renewed it every year

cards.text: So God says He disregarded those fathers. That's a heavy line, friend, but He's not done talking.
So what's different this time? God says what He'll do with His laws in this new covenant.

cards.question: In the new covenant, where does God say He will put His laws?

answers.text: In their minds and on their hearts
On new tablets of stone
On the doorposts of their homes

cards.question: In this new covenant, God also makes a promise about who He will be to His people. What is it?

answers.text: He'll be their God and they'll be His people
He'll be their shield and they'll be His army
He'll be their King and they'll be His servants

cards.text: Then God says, "No longer will each one teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’…" Friend, I've explained my oven timer to every baker who ever walked in here, so that line stops me in my tracks.

cards.question: True or false: In the new covenant, God says only the greatest among them will know Him.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then God says, "For I will forgive their iniquities…" Friend, if I could stamp one line on every cookie box in this bakery, THAT'S the one.

cards.question: God says He will forgive their iniquities. What does He say about their sins?

answers.text: He will remember them no more
He will count them one by one
He will remember them for a season

cards.text: The writer drives it home: by speaking of a new covenant, God has made the first one obsolete. And believe me, I know what it's like when a shiny new stamper shows up on the counter and the old one gets slid to the back of the junk drawer.

cards.question: What does the writer say will happen to what is obsolete and aging?

answers.text: It will soon disappear
It will stand beside the new
It will be kept forever
